# linux_command (Resource)

Runs shell scripts with `/bin/sh` when the resource is created, updated or destroyed, for anything the other resources do not cover. Scripts are sent on standard input, never on a command line, and get an empty standard input themselves.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "linux_command" "swap" {
  create = <<-EOT
    fallocate -l "$SIZE" /swapfile
    chmod 600 /swapfile
    mkswap /swapfile
    swapon /swapfile
  EOT
  read   = "swapon --show=NAME,SIZE --noheadings | grep /swapfile"
  delete = "swapoff /swapfile && rm -f /swapfile"

  environment = {
    SIZE = "2G"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `create` (String) Script run when the resource is created. Changing it runs `update` when set, and replaces the resource otherwise.

### Optional

- `delete` (String) Script run when the resource is destroyed, with the environment and working directory in the state.
- `environment` (Map of String) Environment variables exported to the scripts. Changing it runs `update` when set, and replaces the resource otherwise.
- `read` (String) Script run on refresh, whose standard output becomes `output`. When it exits with a non-zero status, the resource is considered gone and Terraform plans to create it again.
- `triggers` (Map of String) Arbitrary values that run `update`, or replace the resource, when they change.
- `update` (String) Script run when `create`, `environment`, `working_directory` or `triggers` change. Without it, such changes replace the resource.
- `working_directory` (String) Directory the scripts run in. Changing it runs `update` when set, and replaces the resource otherwise.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Random identifier.
- `output` (String) Standard output of `read` when set, of the last `create` or `update` otherwise.
